podcast.body: Released in the summer of 1975, this song reached number one on both the country charts and the Billboard Hot 100. Described as the "epitome of the new country that really isn't country at all," it's about a displaced cowboy and features "lots of strings." Glenn Campbell performed it live at the CMAs the same year John Denver won Entertainer of the Year. Larry Weiss won the CMA Song of the Year for it in 1976. "Rhyne Stone cowboy, lots of strings released in the summer of 1975, number one on the country charts, number one on the Billboard Hot 100."
This breezy groove from 1975 was defeated by Captain & Tennille's "Love Will Keep Us Together" for the year-end title. "Glenn Campbell's Rhyne Stone Cowboy."

podcast.body: This song was a number one hit on the pop charts in 1975, and its country leanings were compared to Olivia Newton-John's "sort of country" status, highlighting the blurred lines of genre in the mid-70s. "Glenn Campbell's Rhyne Stone Calboy, which was also number one of the pop charts."
